transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-07-09 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~48 minutes | Recording: auto
Attendees: Maya Lin (Redwood AE), Daniel Ortiz (Redwood SE); Claire Bennett (NorthHarbor), Ravi Shah (NorthHarbor), Tommy Lee (NorthHarbor)

Summary: Quickwalk of Redwood Console and API controls for request storage and PII redaction. Focus on ephemeral vs persistent request storage toggles, redaction pipelines (regex + ML), KMS/HSM for keying, and how Optimize suggests batching that respects retention policies. Customer asked about audit logs, exportability, and demo of turning off request storage at runtime.

Topics: Console toggles, API headers for storage, redact-on-ingest, retention windows, SOC2/KMS, POC steps

-- Transcript --
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on this account. We've got Daniel from our SE team, and we were planning a 40-ish minute walkthrough of the storage and redaction controls in Console and via API. Can you hear me okay?
[00:06] Claire (NorthHarbor): Yep loud and clear, thanks.
[00:12] Daniel (Redwood SE): Quick intro — I'll demo the Console toggles and then show the API/SDK calls, and finish with how Optimize flags batching/caching tradeoffs when you have strict retention.
[00:18] Ravi (NorthHarbor): Happy with that. Primary ask: we need to be able to claim no user-level prompts are stored for certain classes of requests, and to have logs that remain redacted for audit — also how we can integrate our HSM.
[00:28] Tommy (NorthHarbor): And timeline — if POC looks good we want a month-long pilot in Prod-like env.

[00:45] Maya (Redwood): Got it. Two core levers — 'Request storage' mode (ephemeral | persistent) and 'Redaction pipeline' (none | regex | ml-pii). In Console that's a toggle per-route and you can override at call-time with an API header: X-Redwood-Request-Storage: ephemeral. We'll demo both.
[00:59] Daniel (Redwood SE): One note — ephemeral means we don't persist request bodies or KV-level caches beyond the request lifecycle, but we still write minimal telemetry (latency/metrics) for SLOs. Those metrics don't contain user content.

[01:20] Claire (NorthHarbor): So telemetry is allowed but not the prompts. Good. What about logs from model outputs — are they redacted too?
[01:27] Daniel (Redwood SE): Yes you can chain redaction on outputs as well. Two stages: ingest-time (drop or mask inputs) and post-output redaction (mask outputs). The Console lets you create a pipeline combining regex patterns, built-in PII detectors (ML), and a custom replace rule. There is also an API param redact_rules=[...].

[01:55] Ravi (NorthHarbor): Say we want guaranteed non-retention for a subset of endpoints — must be enforced server-side. How do we assert that to auditors?
[02:02] Maya (Redwood): We provide configs + an audit trail. The audit log shows config changes, who toggled ephemeral storage, and a policy snapshot. We can also export a compliance package: timestamped policy, s3 export of logs with keys masked, and a statement of no user data persisted for requests tagged ephemeral. We'll attach the SOC2 appendix showing log retention practices.

[02:30] Tommy (NorthHarbor): Can you show the Console?
[02:37] Daniel (Redwood SE): Yup — switching to screen. (UI noises and brief screen navigation)
[02:55] Daniel (Redwood SE): Here is the Routes page. You can click an individual route and toggle Request Storage: Persistent, Ephemeral (Drop inputs), or Ephemeral (Mask inputs). The mask option runs through regex or ML detector before storing. Note: regex runs first, then ML, then custom replace.
[03:20] Claire (NorthHarbor): Can we upload our own regex list? We have patterns that are company-specific.
[03:26] Daniel (Redwood SE): Yes — you can upload a CSV of patterns or paste them into the UI and set priority. They’re evaluated locally in the ingestion pipeline. (small pause) sometimes the UI auto-corrects special characters so watch escape sequences — caught us once in prod demos, ha.
[03:50] Maya (Redwood): That’s a good candid note — the Console escapes backslashes which can surprise folks, so for large pattern sets we recommend API upload.
[04:05] Claire (NorthHarbor): Show the API header flow please.
[04:12] Daniel (Redwood SE): Sure — curl example: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -H 'X-Redwood-Request-Storage: ephemeral' -d '{"prompt":"...","redact_rules":[{"type":"regex","pattern":"NH-\\d{6}"}]}'
[04:38] Tommy (NorthHarbor): Does that header supersede route-level settings?
[04:42] Daniel (Redwood SE): Yes, call-time header can override route setting if the policy allows overrides. Admins can lock a route to prevent overrides. If locked, header is ignored and audit will show attempted override.

[05:05] Ravi (NorthHarbor): About keys — we need to use our KMS/HSM for encryption of persistent logs. How does that integrate?
[05:12] Maya (Redwood): We support customer-managed keys — you can bring your own (KMS) via the Private or Dedicated offering. For hosted, we offer envelope encryption with optional customer-provided keys via cloud-KMS. We can show the KMS integration doc after.
[05:28] Claire (NorthHarbor): Any latency impacts when redaction is enabled? We need sub-200ms 95th for many calls.
[05:33] Daniel (Redwood SE): Regex redaction is negligible (<5ms usually). ML-based PII detection adds overhead: depends on model size of the detector, but typical is +20–40ms for our light PII detector. If latency is critical, Optimize recommends routing through a local detector or pre-token masking and it will show token-level cost/latency tradeoffs in the Console.

[06:05] Maya (Redwood): Quick demo of Optimize: you can open the Optimize tab and it will analyze your route historic traffic and recommend a batching window that respects your retention policy — e.g., it will not recommend cross-request caching for ephemeral routes.
[06:26] (short pause, typing)
[06:40] Daniel (Redwood SE): Now I'll show a live PII redaction demo — sending a synthetic request with a NorthHarbor policy ID and SSN-like number.
[06:51] [07:00] Daniel (Redwood SE): curl POST with header X-Redwood-Request-Storage: ephemeral and redact_rules including the regex for NH-\\d{6} and SSN mask pattern. Response shows masked output in the Console log view and no request body in persistent logs.
[07:18] Claire (NorthHarbor): I see in the Console the preview of stored record — it says 'masked' in the content column. Is the full unmasked content ever available to admins?
[07:26] Daniel (Redwood SE): Only if you configure 'mask -> store masked with key' and if you allow unmask via KMS access controls. Default ephemeral mode drop means no unmask path exists — once dropped it's gone.

[07:45] Ravi (NorthHarbor): Can we get a forensic export if regulators ask?
[07:50] Maya (Redwood): Forensic exports follow your retention policy. If you set persistent+masked, you can export masked logs. If ephemeral/dropped there's nothing to export. For audits we provide config history and scrubbed telemetry. We also have an endpoint for signed attestations of retention settings at a point in time.

[08:12] Tommy (NorthHarbor): About RBAC — who can toggle ephemeral at route level?
[08:18] Daniel (Redwood SE): RBAC allows roles: admin, config-editor, auditor. Only admins can lock/unlock route overrides. Config-editors can change rules but cannot change keying/KMS settings. Auditor role gets read-only audit logs.

[08:36] Claire (NorthHarbor): Are there any gotchas for multi-tenant setups? We are running multiple business units.
[08:42] Maya (Redwood): Use Dedicated or Private for strict tenant isolation. We support per-tenant KMS bindings and per-tenant retention policies. Also recommend separate routes and model pins per BU to avoid accidental cross-serve caching.

[09:05] Daniel (Redwood SE): Going to show a quick POC manifest: route config JSON snippet — note the field: "request_storage": "ephemeral", "redaction": {"rules": [ {"type":"regex","pattern":"NH-\\\\d{6}","action":"mask"}, {"type":"pii_ml","sensitivity":"high","action":"mask"} ] } and a lock: "allow_override": false.
[09:40] Claire (NorthHarbor): The double escaping is confusing when copy/pasting from UI to API.
[09:45] Daniel (Redwood SE): Yup apologies — Console shows human-readable form, API needs proper JSON escaping. We'll send an example manifest.

[10:02] [10:20] (slight crosstalk)
[10:35] Ravi (NorthHarbor): What about stored embeddings — we use embeddings heavily. Do we consider embeddings PII?
[10:42] Daniel (Redwood SE): Good question. Embeddings are treated as derived artifacts. If you mark a route as ephemeral, embeddings are not stored. If persistent, we recommend hashing IDs and masking any associated metadata. We also provide an embeddings retention toggle in the Console. Optimize flags when embeddings can be cached safely vs when they should be TTL'd.

[11:05] Tommy (NorthHarbor): Are there API audit endpoints we can poll to verify no content persisted?
[11:11] Maya (Redwood): Yes — we provide an Audit API that returns config snapshots and attempted override logs. You can integrate it into your monitoring.

[11:28] Claire (NorthHarbor): Can you confirm backup snapshots — if data is dropped, could it exist in backups?
[11:34] Daniel (Redwood SE): Our design avoids writing ephemeral request bodies to persistent storage, so backups won't have them. We do backup system metadata and config. For extra assurance we can show the pipeline diagram and include a signed statement for auditors.

[12:05] (typing / short pause)
[12:24] Daniel (Redwood SE): I'm going to toggle a route to 'persistent masked' then run a sample query so you can see how masking and KMS-based unmasking would work (demoled).
[12:40] [13:00] Claire (NorthHarbor): Looking at the masked store: what's the retention window config?
[13:05] Daniel (Redwood SE): You can set retention per-route: 7 days, 30 days, 90 days, custom up to X years depending on contract. For Dedicated we support enterprise custom retention. Default for hosted masked is 30 days.

[13:30] Ravi (NorthHarbor): For legal we need 90 days masked, but the raw content never stored. Sounds like persistent+masked for 90 days.
[13:36] Maya (Redwood): Correct. We'll provision POC with that setting.

[13:50] Tommy (NorthHarbor): Any impact on cost? We need a cost estimate for masked vs ephemeral per 100k requests.
[13:57] Maya (Redwood): Ephemeral is cheapest since no storage. Masked has storage and encryption cost — we'll send a cost spreadsheet for 100k request profiles. Optimize will also estimate token-level cost differences when you enable pre-token redaction vs post-output redaction.

[14:25] Claire (NorthHarbor): Walk me through a worst-case scenario — if a dev flips a route to persistent without audit, how do we detect it?
[14:33] Daniel (Redwood SE): Audit trail captures the change and triggers a policy alert if it violates guard rails. You can configure Slack/email hooks for any change from ephemeral->persistent. If locked, only admins can do it and it requires 2FA.

[15:00] Maya (Redwood): Quick pivot — show sample code for SDK with ephemeral flag. (Daniel shares code)
[15:06] Daniel (Redwood SE): JS SDK snippet:
const client = new RedwoodClient({ key: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY })
await client.generate({ route: 'nh-sensitive', prompt: '...', metadata:{}, options:{ requestStorage: 'ephemeral', redactRules:[ {type:'regex', pattern:'NH-\\\\d{6}'} ] } })

[15:36] Claire (NorthHarbor): We use Python — can you send a Python sample?
[15:39] Maya (Redwood): We'll include both and a curl quickstart.

[16:00] (small pause)
[16:18] Tommy (NorthHarbor): A question on incident response — if we detect leakage, can we retroactively redact stored outputs?
[16:24] Daniel (Redwood SE): You can run a retroactive redaction job on stored logs — it creates a re-ingest job that rewrites masked content and records the action in audit logs. If raw content was never stored (ephemeral) there's nothing to redact. Note: retroactive redaction can't unring previously sent webhook payloads — you need to rotate downstream systems.

[17:00] (brief laughter)
[17:10] Claire (NorthHarbor): Do you support PII classification models in different languages? We have EU and APAC customers.
[17:18] Daniel (Redwood SE): Yes, ML detectors support major languages, regional sensitivity levels can be tuned. We'll include the ML detector coverage matrix.

[17:40] Ravi (NorthHarbor): For the POC we want: 1) route locked ephemeral for certain endpoints; 2) a persistent masked route for audit purposes (90d); 3) KMS integration for masked unmask-by-role. Is that doable?
[17:52] Maya (Redwood): Totally. That's what we'll provision. Daniel will set up two routes with those settings in the sandbox.

[18:10] Daniel (Redwood SE): I'll note the manifest names and we'll push them to the POC account.

[18:30] (typing)
[19:00] Claire (NorthHarbor): One more ask — can you show how Optimize would flag a regression if we change redaction rules and that causes output drift?
[19:10] Daniel (Redwood SE): Yep — Optimize can bind an eval set to a route and track quality metrics. If redaction changes lead to meaningful distributional changes in responses, Optimize will surface regression alerts and can roll back to previous model or redaction snapshot during canary.

[19:42] Tommy (NorthHarbor): Does rollback also revert storage settings?
[19:46] Maya (Redwood): Rollback can revert route config snapshots including storage and redaction rules if you include them in the rollout. We recommend canaries for config changes.

[20:10] Claire (NorthHarbor): Ok let's recap next steps.
[20:16] Maya (Redwood): Recap: 1) We will send SOC2 + KMS doc. 2) Daniel will provision POC sandbox with two routes (ephemeral locked, persistent+masked 90d + KMS unmask). 3) We'll share sample SDK snippets and cost estimate. 4) Schedule benchmark week-of 2025-07-21.
[20:36] Claire (NorthHarbor): Sounds good. Ravi/Tommy — any remaining security blockers?
[20:42] Ravi (NorthHarbor): Just to confirm we get a signed attestation for the ephemeral drop behavior and the manifest.
[20:48] Maya (Redwood): Yes we can provide a signed statement.

[21:00] (closing notes)
[21:12] Maya (Redwood): Thanks everyone — we'll follow up by email with the links.
[21:20] Claire (NorthHarbor): Thanks, appreciate the demo.

End of meeting.
